title: Zero-Trust Architecture
description: Learn zero-trust architecture principles for securing microservices.

data.text: Zero trust is a security model that assumes no implicit trust, even for internal services. Google's BeyondCorp and NIST SP 800-207 are foundational zero-trust frameworks adopted by companies like Coinbase and Salesforce for microservices security.

Zero trust architecture (ZTA) is based on the principle 'never trust, always verify.' Every request must be authenticated and authorized, regardless of where it originates. Identity and device posture become the primary security boundaries.

data.title: Zero Trust Implementation Steps
items: Identify all resources and data flows
Implement strong authentication for all access
Monitor and log all access for anomaly detection

data.title: Google BeyondCorp
data.text: Google's BeyondCorp eliminated the corporate VPN by requiring device and user verification for every access, even from the internal network. This zero-trust model is now widely adopted for microservices.

data.title: Example: Zero Trust Policy
data.content: A zero-trust policy for microservices communication.
data.code:
# Zero Trust Policy

# Rule 1: All traffic must be authenticated
# Every request must have a valid JWT or mTLS certificate

# Rule 2: Least privilege access
# Service A can only call Service B's /orders endpoint
# Service A cannot call Service B's /admin endpoint

# Rule 3: Encrypt all traffic
# TLS 1.3 for all external and internal communication

# Rule 4: Continuous verification
# Monitor for anomalies: unusual access patterns,
# new IPs, or privilege escalation

items.question: Is zero trust realistic for microservices?
items.answer: Yes, but it requires investment. Start with mTLS for service-to-service communication and JWT for user authentication. Add device posture and continuous verification over time.

items.question: What is the biggest zero trust challenge?
items.answer: Operational complexity. Managing identities, certificates, and policies at scale requires automation and tooling like service meshes and identity providers.

items.question: Does zero trust replace firewalls?
items.answer: No. Zero trust complements network security. Firewalls protect the perimeter; zero trust protects resources regardless of network location.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Zero trust means never trusting any request by default
Every request must be authenticated and authorized
mTLS and service meshes enable zero trust for microservices
data.takeaway: Zero trust is the future of microservices security; adopt it incrementally starting with mTLS.
